description:
**Blocked by d06.1 (VDom core including %VCursor{} struct must
exist). Read deck §8 "Cursor as a VNode" before starting.**

The terminal cursor becomes a zero-width `%VCursor{style: :bar |
:block | :underline}` leaf. The painter stamps `{row, col, style}`
into LineBuf metadata; LineBuf.finalize/1 returns
`{iodata, cursor_or_nil}`. Renderer.render/4 derives cursor_seq
from the stamped position when present, emits hide-cursor when
absent.

**Read first:**
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/renderer.ex` — find the
  `cursor_seq` parameter on `render/3,4`. Today it's an opaque
  binary built by the caller; this ticket keeps that interface
  but moves construction into the painter pipeline.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/render_loop.ex` — the
  `{:render, lines, cursor_seq}` message shape. Stays the same.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/input.ex` — the
  current cursor positioning logic (search for
  `cursor` and screen-coord arithmetic). d06.7 only handles
  the cursor primitive; d06.11 converts the rest of Input.
- The new VDom modules from d06.1.

**Cursor sequences (existing constants in renderer.ex):**
- Show + position: `"\\e[?25h\\e[#{row + 1};#{col + 1}H"` (1-based).
- Hide: `"\\e[?25l"`.
- Style (DECSCUSR): `:bar` `"\\e[5 q"`, `:block` `"\\e[1 q"`,
  `:underline` `"\\e[3 q"`.

**Implementation:**

  - `LineBuf.mark_cursor(buf, style) :: buf` — stamps
    `{line_count, visible_width, style}` into metadata. Last call
    wins.
  - `LineBuf.finalize(buf) :: {iodata, cursor_or_nil}` — returns
    cursor as `{row, col, style}` or `nil`.
  - In `OctoPi.TUI.VDom.Paint`: `paint(%VCursor{style: s}, _w, buf)`
    calls `LineBuf.mark_cursor(buf, s)` and returns buf unchanged
    in line content.
  - In containers (VBox padding rows, VRow inline emission): the
    painter's line/column counters MUST advance through emitted
    bytes (border, padding) before descending into children, so
    cursor coords are correct without any explicit offset math
    by the component.
  - Memo cell shape from d06.1 carries `cursor_offset_or_nil`. On
    cache hit, painter applies the offset to its current line/col
    so the cursor "moves with" the cached subtree.
  - Build `cursor_seq` in `OctoPi.TUI.UI.State.paint/2` (or in
    Interactive's `send_render` wrapper — pick whichever keeps
    the API clean) by formatting `{row, col, style}` into the
    sequences above. `nil` → emit hide sequence.

**Input integration (this ticket — minimal):**
Add a single `%VCursor{style: :bar}` to `Components.Input`'s render
path between the text-before-caret and text-after-caret. The full
Input migration (other surfaces, dropdown, IME) lives in d06.11.

**Acceptance:**
- Unit tests on `LineBuf.mark_cursor/2` and `paint(%VCursor{}, …)`:
  cursor follows nested VBox padding offsets (a VCursor inside a
  VBox(padding_x: 2, padding_y: 1) lands at the correct absolute
  position).
- Multi-VCursor test: a tree with two VCursor leaves emits the
  position of the *last* one painted.
- Absent VCursor: paint returns `cursor: nil`; renderer emits hide
  sequence.
- Memo + cursor: cache the input subtree, advance the cursor by
  one column via setter, paint again — cursor lands at the new
  position even though the memo subtree was a hit. (This exercises
  the `cursor_offset` field in the memo cell.)
- tmux smoke: typing characters in the input keeps the hardware
  cursor under the right glyph; deleting characters keeps it
  positioned correctly; IME composition (use a JP/CN input method)
  shows the cursor at the composition point.
title: Cursor-as-VNode: Input emits VCursor; renderer derives cursor_seq from buffer
